clue.text: Waiter employed on the permanent way?

definitions.text: Waiter employed on the permanent way?

parts.words: Waiter employed on the permanent way?
parts.note: a waiter sets down dishes on tables; read literally the job title describes one who puts down plates, but the permanent way is railway track, so this is a track worker

explanation.surface: A restaurant waiter has somehow ended up working on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'permanent way' is the British term for the finished railway track; the workers who lay and maintain it share a name with someone who sets out plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway workers who lay and maintain track are called by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Hock for a possible future queen

explanation.surface: Selling one's belongings to fund a would-be royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hock' here is not the wine but the slang for leaving goods as security for a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: To hock goods is to pledge them for a loan; in chess the lowliest piece can be promoted to a queen on reaching the far rank.

clue.text: You have no right to tease a friend

indicators.note: no right means the abbreviation for right is dropped from the teasing word

parts.note: to rally someone, in an old sense, is to tease or banter with them

explanation.surface: Someone is told they have no business mocking a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' tells you to remove R (right) from RALLY, the old verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or supporter on one's side is a synonym for a friend.

clue.text: Suffolk town's spectators

parts.note: Eye is a small market town in Suffolk; people watching there would be its witnesses, which is also the name for anyone who sees an event first-hand

explanation.surface: Onlookers gathered in a small East Anglian town.
explanation.walkthrough: Eye is a small market town in Suffolk, in eastern England; the people of that town who watch something become, punningly, those who saw it with their own eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: People who see an event happen and can testify to it are first-hand observers.

clue.text: High priest gets money from India

explanation.surface: A senior cleric is paid in Indian currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Annas was the Jewish high priest before whom Jesus was first brought; the same letters are the plural of an old Indian coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament names Annas as a high priest; former Indian coins worth one-sixteenth of a rupee were annas.

clue.text: Fined at Oxford after two points established

indicators.note: after places the Oxford word behind the compass points in the answer

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
at Oxford colleges a sconce was a penalty, so to be sconced was to be fined

explanation.surface: An undergraduate penalised at Oxford for two misdemeanours becomes settled.
explanation.walkthrough: SCONCE is old Oxford college slang for a fine imposed at dinner, usually paid in ale.
explanation.definitionFit: To be settled firmly and comfortably in a place is to be installed securely there.

clue.text: Final form of bills presented for housework

explanation.surface: Bills are finished off, presented in place of domestic chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housework' is not cleaning but the work of the House, Parliament, whose bills become law in this final form.
explanation.definitionFit: Once passed, a parliamentary bill becomes a statute, and statutes are the output of the legislature.

clue.text: Water-bed was in the van as directed

parts.note: a channel is the bed of a watercourse
to be in the van, the vanguard, is to be at the front, so the person who was there led

explanation.surface: A water-bed was delivered in a van as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is short for vanguard, the front of an army, not a delivery vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Guided or steered along a set route is a synonym for directed.

clue.text: The season for adders ?

parts.note: adders here are not snakes but people who add up figures, so the season belonging to them is named after doing sums

explanation.surface: When is the best time of year to see snakes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'adders' are those who add, that is, people who do sums; the warm season's name splits as a time for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The warm months of the year are the hottest season.

clue.text: No place for an office-party!

parts.note: a political party out of office is said to be in a barren wasteland, the place for those not in government

explanation.surface: A warning that some venue is unsuitable for the work Christmas do.
explanation.walkthrough: An office party here is a political party in office; a party out of power is said, in British political idiom, to be in the barren land.
explanation.definitionFit: A barren uninhabited region is where politicians out of power are said to languish.

clue.text: Its existence in Gilead was questionable

definitions.text: Its existence in Gilead was questionable

parts.words: Its existence in Gilead was questionable
parts.note: Jeremiah asks whether there is any healing ointment in Gilead, so its existence there is literally put as a question

explanation.surface: Doubts are raised about whether something existed in a biblical region.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremiah 8:22 asks, 'Is there no balm in Gilead?' It is a question, so the existence was literally 'questionable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing healing ointment is the substance the prophet asks about.

clue.text: A golfer's idea on crowded course ? It's premeditated

parts.note: a golfer shouts fore as a warning to others, especially on a crowded course
an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A golfer has an idea on a busy course, which turns out to be planned in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: On a crowded course a golfer's warning shout comes first to mind. 'Malice aforethought' is the legal phrase for premeditated intent.
explanation.definitionFit: Planned in advance, as in the legal phrase malice planned beforehand, is premeditated.

clue.text: Original sin dealt with leniently

parts.note: not the theological doctrine but a person's first crime, which courts commonly treat lightly

explanation.surface: A theological doctrine is handled gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original sin' tempts toward theology, but read literally it is simply a first wrongdoing, which a court often punishes lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer's first crime is literally their original sin, and magistrates traditionally show mercy for it.

clue.text: Belittle recipe with date mix

indicators.note: mix tells you to stir the letters of the two words together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a recipe calling for a mixture with dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix' rearranges RECIPE and DATE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage or play down something's worth is to belittle it.

clue.text: Report worker to bookkeeper

parts.note: an account is a report or narrative
a worker is a type of ant, so ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: An employee is reported to the person keeping the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is the crossword staple for ANT, from the worker ants of a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who keeps and audits financial records is a bookkeeper.

clue.text: Odd sort of orbit

explanation.surface: A strange kind of path around a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is peculiar is odd; an orbit that is not circular but elliptical is described with the same word.

clue.text: Cancellation of debt relating to embassy

parts.note: re means concerning or relating to
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: A diplomatic matter concerning writing off a nation's debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgiving a debt or penalty is a pardoning, a release from the obligation.

clue.text: Release money in tree-development

indicators.note: in puts the money letter inside the rearranged tree
development tells you to work the letters of the tree into a new form

parts.note: L stands for pound, from libra, so it can mean money

explanation.surface: Money is released to develop a tree plantation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges TREE as RETE, and 'in' puts L (pound) inside it. 'Release' is read as re-lease, let again.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-lease, to lease a property again is to let it once more.

clue.text: Fleeces blackbirds ?

explanation.surface: Sheep's coats belonging to dark songbirds.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that these birds are black birds, not true blackbirds.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle someone is to fleece them; crows of a common black, colony-nesting kind are black birds.

clue.text: It's rammed, somehow, though far from the bank

indicators.note: somehow tells you the letters reach the answer by some unstated rearrangement

explanation.surface: A boat is rammed, though it is well away from the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges ITS and RAMMED.
explanation.definitionFit: In the middle of a river, away from either shore, is far from the bank.

clue.text: This piece of art work causes talk

definitions.text: This piece of art work causes talk

parts.words: This piece of art work causes talk
parts.note: a genre painting of people chatting is called by this name plus piece, and any object prompting discussion is one too

explanation.surface: An artwork has people talking.
explanation.walkthrough: A conversation piece is both an informal group portrait, a genre of painting, and anything that gets people talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Talk between people is chat, and the painting genre and talking point are named after it.

clue.text: This balance may show inaccuracy

parts.note: in bookkeeping a test listing of debit and credit totals is made to see whether they agree, exposing errors

explanation.surface: A pair of scales may give a faulty reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' suggests weighing scales, but here it is the accountant's trial balance, drawn up to see whether the books agree.
explanation.definitionFit: A test or experiment is a trial, and the accountant's balance is a test of the books.

clue.text: Top put on one in the tropics

definitions.text: Top put on one in the tropics

indicators.note: put on places the top word before the numeral, as in a down clue one piece sits on another

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hat is placed on someone's head in hot countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a pith helmet is headgear worn in hot countries, and the wordplay places TOP on I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun helmet worn in hot climates is a hat put on in the tropics.

clue.text: Sticks up for the self-satisfied

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: gums are adhesives, so to gum things is to stick them

explanation.surface: Someone stands up for complacent people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GUMS (sticks) in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Complacent and pleased with oneself is self-satisfied.

clue.text: Nurse from a graduate hospital

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A nurse comes from a hospital as a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: An amah is a nursemaid in parts of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: In East and South Asia a nursemaid or wet nurse is called by this name.

clue.text: Exhausting place for old actors?

parts.note: read as a wearying place it suggests hard work, but in old theatres the chamber where players put on their costumes took its name from attire

explanation.surface: Acting was a draining business in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausting' suggests weariness, but 'tiring' here is from attire: the old theatre's dressing room.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing room in an old theatre was named from attiring, dressing the players.

clue.text: Brief tariff, partly valid for economic group

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A short tariff is only partly valid for a trade bloc.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'valid for economic group' as the definition, but 'valid for' is a link: the definition is 'economic group', the European Free Trade Association.
explanation.definitionFit: The European Free Trade Association is a trading bloc of European states.

clue.text: Preparing for nudist lunch, got in trouble

indicators.note: trouble tells you the letters of the words before it are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Lunch at a naturist camp went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is fodder, not a link: 'trouble' rearranges LUNCH, GOT and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking one's clothes off is what one does before going naked.
